**A small subset is useful if it preserves the decisions you want to make from it.** For rapid hyperparameter screening, the key question is whether configurations rank similarly on the subset and the larger dataset. Matching one model's accuracy is not enough. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00068) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

Start with stratified and diverse real examples, preserving rare classes, temporal regimes, and valuable edge cases. Error-based scores such as EL2N can highlight informative examples, but high error also identifies mislabeled or corrupted data. Gradient-based selection aims to preserve training influence more directly, with its own estimation cost.

**Coresets and dataset distillation differ.** A coreset selects real examples. Distillation optimizes synthetic examples to reproduce aspects of training behavior. Synthetic data may work for one architecture or initialization and transfer poorly to another.

There is no general guarantee that 5% of rows retains 99% of full-data performance. Use progressively larger confirmation runs and a final full evaluation for promising configurations. Measure compute saved, ranking agreement, and rare-slice quality. The subset is a screening instrument whose reliability must be checked.

**Technical details and references.**

No selection rule guarantees 99% of full-data accuracy from 5% of rows. Build a stratified/diverse baseline subset, then compare error-based scores such as EL2N or gradient-matching selections at matched size. Keep rare classes, temporal regimes, and high-value edge cases represented. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00068) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

Hard examples can be informative or mislabeled; blindly retaining the highest error scores can concentrate noise. Dataset distillation creates synthetic training examples optimized to approximate training behavior, whereas coreset selection chooses real examples; they have different risks and costs.

Use the subset for fast screening, then confirm promising configurations on progressively larger data and finally the full validation regime. Measure hyperparameter ranking agreement, not only one subset-trained model's accuracy.
